To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
insulin stimulates protein synthesis in rat liver, and that this is due to a direct effect of the hormone on the microsomal fraction.
insulin increases the rate of protein synthesis by liver microsomes, but that this increase is not due to an increase in the rate of amino acid activation by soluble enzymes.
insulin stimulates protein synthesis by liver microsomes in vivo and in vitro, and that insulin deficiency results in a decreased capacity for microsomal protein synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of insulin on the incorporation of amino acids into protein of liver microsomal fractions.
the effects of insulin and alloxan on the incorporation of radioactive amino acids into protein of rat liver microsomes.

the effects of diabetes and insulin upon the ability of liver microsomal preparations from rats to incorporate amino acids into protein in the presence of a soluble activating factor from the same animal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the insulin effect on amino acid incorporation is specific for microsomes and that it may be a consequence of insulin effect upon the synthesis of microsomal components.
insulin is necessary for the maintenance of normal microsomal protein synthesis in vivo, and that this effect of insulin is mediated by the microsomal membrane.
insulin stimulates amino acid incorporation into liver microsomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amino acid incorporating capacity in vitro of liver microsomal protein synthesis is decreased by severe alloxan diabetes and restored by insulin.
insulin has a specific effect upon the microsome system, which is not mediated by soluble factors, and that this is not a direct effect of insulin in vitro.
the amino acid incorporating capacity is reduced in liver microsomes of diabetic rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microsomal amino acid incorporating system is not a good marker for insulin deficiency in diabetes.
insulin has a profound effect on the microsomal amino acid incorporating system.
insulin can be used to treat diabetes.
